goal: Drive current-source AKS RP e2e quality normalization to completion: every active scenario carrier is standalone, officially grounded, mutation-safe, fixture- and cleanup-owned, and backed by accepted staging proof before direct origin/dev integration or an exact external blocker.
strategy: Let the existing scenario-normalization task and aks-explorer directly own quality-normalization selection, repair, staging proof, and origin/dev integration.
Ground every normalized carrier in official Learn or Azure REST API contracts plus checked-in design evidence, using implementation source only as supporting evidence.
Keep a bounded three-to-five-leaf normalization frontier moving while preserving exact pipeline, capability, approval, and environment waits.
Use bounded controllers to declare current work; use the canonical task projection to observe live state.
Have May and app-ops monitor throughput and integrity, repair orchestration or runtime failures, and return domain judgment to the app rather than performing AKS normalization work themselves.

planning.focus: Drive the existing scenario-normalization resource against clean current origin/dev while May monitors execution, repairs control-plane issues, and prevents the bounded quality frontier from stalling.
successCriteria: scenario-normalization remains the single quality-frontier owner and keeps three to five useful domain leaves represented whenever eligible work exists.
Every active scenario carrier has current-source structural review, official contract grounding, explicit target and mutation gates, fixture and cleanup ownership, and accepted staging proof.
A row leaves the frontier only after its tested change is integrated into origin/dev or an exact typed external blocker or escalation is durably represented.
The clean-origin/dev strict inventory and required full repository check pass, and every current quality row is covered without stale terminal residue.
May and app-ops repair task integrity, delivery, authentication, watcher, and controller faults without taking ownership of AKS domain implementation.
